title: The Tribe of Dan
lead: The tribe descended from Jacob's son Dan, first given land near the coast, later moved to Laish at the springs of the Jordan, which it renamed Dan. The town became Israel's northern limit and the site of one of Jeroboam's golden calves.

sections.b: Dan was the first son of Bilhah, Rachel's servant (Genesis 30:5–6), whose name means "he judged." Jacob said, "Dan will judge his people," and called him a snake by the road (Genesis 49:16–17); Moses called him a lion's cub (Deuteronomy 33:22). Dan's land lay between Judah, Ephraim and the Philistine coast (Joshua 19:40–46), but the tribe could not hold it (Judges 1:34; Joshua 19:47) and most of it moved north to Laish (Judges 18). Samson came from the Danites who stayed (Judges 13:2). The city of Dan became the northern end of "from Dan to Beersheba" and the site of Jeroboam's golden calf (1 Kings 12:29–30), which Amos condemns (Amos 8:14). Dan is missing from the tribes sealed in Revelation 7:4–8, which some early Christians linked with a belief that the Antichrist would come from Dan. Excavations at Tel Dan have uncovered the ancient city, its gate, a large sacred platform, and the Tel Dan Stele naming the "House of David."
